fix.consent.title: Let an agent work on {project}?
fix.consent.plain_project: To fix this project, Michel has Claude Code work on a copy of your project: an AI (artificial intelligence) made by the company Anthropic. The files of that copy that the AI reads go out over the Internet, to Anthropic. If Michel recognizes a key or a password in them, the AI does not start before you answer; a secret it does not recognize can go out with the files. Nothing changes in your real project without your approval.
fix.consent.plain_server: To help fix this server, Michel can ask Claude Code, an AI (artificial intelligence) made by the company Anthropic. It receives, over the Internet, the versions and settings read on this server, the problem found and your messages. Michel removes what it recognizes as a secret; a secret it does not recognize can go out. The AI never connects to the server and nothing is run on it without your approval.

servers.intro: Michel reads your servers over a secure connection, without installing or changing anything there, and tells you whether they have a known flaw.

servers.discover.loading: Michel is reading the connections saved on this computer and your PhpStorm projects.
servers.discover.none: Michel found no new server in your saved connections or in your projects.
servers.discover.none_hint: Add it by hand: you need its address, the user name to connect with and the access number (almost always 22). Your host can give them to you.
servers.discover.authorize: Adding this server allows Michel to connect to it.

servers.discover.name: Name (for you)
servers.discover.key_only: Michel connects only with a key (a secret file that replaces the password), held by a program on your computer made for that (the SSH agent). Never with a password. Best is a separate account for Michel on the server, with its own key: ask whoever manages your server.

servers.hostkey.loading: Michel is reading the fingerprint the server shows.
servers.hostkey.first: The server shows this fingerprint. Compare it with the one your host gives (or ask whoever manages the server to type: ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub). If it is the same, confirm it: Michel will then connect only if the server shows this fingerprint.
servers.hostkey.pinned: This fingerprint is already confirmed: Michel connects to this server only.
servers.hostkey.changed: Warning: the server shows a fingerprint other than the one you confirmed.
servers.hostkey.changed_why: It may be an attack: someone is pretending to be your server. It may also come from a reinstall. Michel did not connect and changed nothing. Check with your host before replacing the fingerprint.
servers.hostkey.replace_ok: I know why the key changed (for example, I reinstalled the server) and I checked the new fingerprint with my host.
servers.sheet.loading: Michel is opening the server's sheet.
servers.sheet.checking: Michel is checking the server… this can take a minute.
servers.sheet.source: Michel can tell whether the software installed on your server is up to date, using a public list of known flaws. That list, called {key}, is turned off for now, so Michel does not say. Turning it on allows Michel to download it from the Internet.
servers.sheet.source_open: Open the Sources page to turn it on
servers.sheet.no_flaws: No known flaw on this server.
servers.sheet.no_flaws_unchecked: Michel has not checked this server yet: he knows nothing of its flaws.
servers.sheet.mitigation: reduces the risk, does not fix
servers.sheet.fix_report_only: This server is set to "Report": change its level in the settings for Michel to prepare a fix.
servers.sheet.php_built: installed separately, not by the system
servers.sheet.no_projects: No project linked to this server.
servers.sheet.unseen_none: Michel could read everything at the last check.
servers.sheet.unseen_hint: Michel never forces a refused read. If it matters, ask whoever manages your server to give read rights to the account Michel connects with, then check again.
servers.sheet.backups.one: Michel keeps {n} file copy of this server ({size}), encrypted, on your computer, for 90 days.
servers.sheet.backups.other: Michel keeps {n} file copies of this server ({size}), encrypted, on your computer, for 90 days.
servers.sheet.backups_server: On the server, the copies stay in /var/lib/michel/backups/ and ~/.michel/backups/: Michel never deletes them. Empty these folders yourself when you no longer need them.
servers.settings.title: Settings
servers.settings.level: What Michel does with the flaws
servers.settings.auto: Fix the known risky settings on his own (level 3)
servers.settings.auto_hint: Only PHP settings planned by Michel's rules, never a software update nor an agent proposal. Michel first tests the configuration, tries on the preprod if there is one, then checks the site. Works only if Michel runs the scripts himself.
servers.settings.executor.user: You: Michel prepares the scripts, you run them on the server yourself.
servers.settings.executor.michel: Michel: after your approval, Michel runs the script over his secure connection and follows each step.
servers.settings.sudo.none: Michel never uses sudo on this server.
servers.settings.sudo.nopasswd: Michel may use sudo without a password (administrator rights) for a fix: simulate an update, run or undo the script, read back its backups. Never to check the server. At the last level, if he fixes on his own, a script runs without your click.
servers.settings.site_sentence: After each fix, Michel opens {url} from your computer to check that the site answers.
servers.settings.site_none: Without an address, Michel cannot see the site go down after a fix: he undoes nothing for that, and he never fixes on his own.
servers.settings.preprod_sentence: Fixes are first tried on {name}; production is only offered after a full success there.
servers.settings.preprod_empty: No preprod: fixes are made directly here.
servers.settings.hds_note: An HDS server holds health data: Michel never sends an AI agent there, and prepares only his own fixes.
servers.ai.title: AI agent for this server
servers.ai.of_preprod: The agent receives the inventory of the preprod {name}: the consent below is about it.
servers.ai.given: Consent given on {date}: the agent may read the masked versions and settings of {name}.
servers.ai.missing: No consent: Michel prepares his fixes alone. He calls on the agent only for the cases to study.
servers.ai.give: See what leaves and give consent
servers.ai.revoked: Consent withdrawn: no agent works on this server any more.
servers.unknown.title: An earlier fix was left without an answer
servers.unknown.body: On this server, a script stopped without Michel knowing what it changed. Until this is settled, no other fix can be prepared here. Check the server yourself, then click "I checked the server" in that fix.
servers.unknown.body_preprod: On your preprod {name} (your trial server), a script stopped without Michel knowing what it changed. The fixes of this server start on that preprod: until this is settled, no other can be prepared here. Check that preprod yourself, then click "I checked the server" in its fix.
servers.remove.title: Remove {name} from Michel?
servers.remove.body: Nothing is done on the server. Michel forgets its sheet and takes back the network rules he wrote for it; the file copies already made stay on the server.
servers.remove.rules_not_removed: The server is removed, but Michel could not take it out of his rules file. To do it by hand, ask whoever manages your computer: in network.allow, the entries target.ssh and target.http.
srvfix.for_production: This fix is first tried on the preprod, before the production {name}.
srvfix.mitigation: Reduces the risk, does not fix: this setting closes a way in, but the flaw stays open until PHP is upgraded.
srvfix.snapshot.title: First: a snapshot
srvfix.snapshot.body: Make a snapshot of this server (a full copy, from your account at your host; ask them if you cannot find it). A software update has no undo script: your snapshot is the only way back.
srvfix.approve_hint.michel: Approve: Michel sends exactly this script over his secure connection and follows each step. If the site has an address and stops answering, he undoes it at once, except a software update: only your snapshot (a full copy of the server) takes you back then.
srvfix.approve_hint.user: Approve: Michel gives you the script to run on the server yourself. He does not connect to apply it.
srvfix.approve_snapshot_first: Tick "Snapshot done" first to be able to approve.
srvfix.approving: Michel is running the script on the server…
srvfix.copy_failed: The browser could not copy: select the text and copy it yourself.
srvfix.rollback.config: The script itself puts the kept files back and reloads PHP if a step fails after the change. Later, the "Undo" script puts the server back as it was.
srvfix.rollback.package: No script can undo a software update: the way back is your snapshot.
srvfix.user.title: Your turn to run the script
srvfix.user.body: Copy the "Apply" script, run it on the server, then click "I applied it": Michel then checks the site and the server. Keep the "Undo" script at hand.
srvfix.user.root: This script must be run with the server's administrator rights (called "root"): otherwise it stops before changing anything.
srvfix.handover.ready: You changed the setting: Michel can now run this same script for you, without you having to copy it.
srvfix.handover.title: Let Michel run this script?
srvfix.handover.body: Michel will connect to the server and run exactly the script you validated, with administrator rights (root). Then he checks your site and the server. The script does not change, but this is a new validation from you: if it has changed since, Michel does not run it.
srvfix.handover.body_plain: Michel will connect to the server and run exactly the script you validated, with the rights of your connection. Then he checks your site and the server. The script does not change, but this is a new validation from you: if it has changed since, Michel does not run it.
srvfix.handover.settings: Michel cannot run this script for now. Two ways: ask the person who looks after the server to run it, or allow Michel to do it in the server's settings ("Who runs the scripts": Michel; and if the script needs administrator rights, also allow "sudo"), then come back here: a button will appear.
srvfix.handover.busy: Michel is running the script and follows each step. It can take a minute.
srvfix.applying: Michel is checking the site and the server…
srvfix.auto: Approved automatically by your rules, not run yet: Michel runs it as soon as he can reach the server.
srvfix.approved: Approved: Michel is running the script.
srvfix.running: The script is running on the server. Each step shows here.
srvfix.unknown.title: Michel cannot tell what the script changed
srvfix.unknown.body: The script did not answer in time, or the connection dropped. Michel guessed nothing and undid nothing. Look at the server yourself (the changed file, PHP, the site). When done, tell Michel: he closes this fix and you can prepare another one.
srvfix.restore.title: Restore your snapshot now
srvfix.restore.body: The software update went wrong and no script can undo it. Restore the snapshot you made at your host, then check the server.
srvfix.backup_hint: To put a file back by hand: copy the backup over the changed file (cp <backup> <file>), then reload PHP.
srvfix.done.proven_fixed: Fixed: the new check no longer sees the problem.
srvfix.done.inconclusive: The script ran, but Michel could not prove the fix.
srvfix.done.refused: You refused this proposal: Michel ran nothing.
srvfix.done.superseded: A newer fix replaced this one.
srvfix.no_agent_chat: Michel prepares this fix alone, from his rules: no agent, nothing to discuss.
projsrv.title: Servers of this project
projsrv.none: No server linked to this project. On the Servers page, "Find my servers" reads the project's PhpStorm settings.
servers.level.3.warn: Note: a fix Michel prepared, even on your request, can then run on its own when it keeps these rules.
fix.intro_server: For a server, Michel prepares the usual planned fixes himself. An agent only helps discuss a specific case and changes nothing on its own. Nothing changes on the server without your approval or a rule you turned on yourself.
srvfix.scripts_unreadable: Michel cannot show these scripts as they are (unreadable text). Run nothing: prepare a new fix.
logs.title: Logs
logs.intro: A log is a file where your server writes down what went wrong. Michel can read it from time to time to tell you when a new error shows up. It changes nothing on the server and never keeps a line of the log.
logs.loading: Michel is looking at the logs of this server…
logs.copy_failed: Copying did not work: select the command by hand.
logs.format.json: Application that records its errors in JSON format (ask whoever installed your site)
logs.format.text: Other text file (you say how to spot an error)
logs.status.resolved: Not seen again for a while
logs.status.ignored: Ignored: Michel no longer warns you about this one
logs.sources.title: The logs Michel reads
logs.sources.none: Michel does not read any log of this server yet. Until you add one, it reads nothing and so cannot report any error to you.
logs.sources.active_hint: Untick to make Michel stop reading it. The errors already seen stay on screen.
logs.sources.remove_hint: Michel forgets this log and its errors. The file stays untouched on the server.
logs.sources.remove_body: Michel forgets this log and the errors it took from it. The file stays untouched on the server. You can add it again later.
logs.add.title: Add a log
logs.add.find: Look for logs on this server
logs.add.find_hint: Michel looks at what it already knows about this server and at the usual places. It creates nothing: you choose.
logs.add.none: Michel found nothing to suggest. You can give the location of a log yourself below.
logs.add.none_simple: Michel found nothing to suggest. To give the location of a log yourself, turn on the advanced mode in the settings.
logs.add.manual: Or give the location of a log yourself
logs.add.path: Where the file is on the server
logs.add.path_hint: For example /var/log/php/error.log. You can put a star (*) only in the file name, like laravel-*.log for one file per day.
logs.add.format: What type of log is it?
logs.add.level_field: Name of the field that tells how serious it is
logs.add.level_field_hint: In a JSON log, the seriousness (error, warning…) sits in a field. Write its name, often level.
logs.add.channel_field: Name of the field that tells which part of the application is concerned (optional: you can leave it empty)
logs.add.pattern_hint: Michel keeps the lines that contain this word, for example ERROR.
logs.add.try_hint: Michel reads this log once and shows you what it would keep. Nothing is stored, and nothing is watched until you click “Read this log”.
logs.add.start_hint: Michel starts reading this log regularly and warns you about new errors. It starts from now: older errors in the file are not read.
logs.add.trying: Michel is reading the log on the server…
logs.try.title: Here is what Michel would keep from this log
logs.try.partial: The log is big: Michel read only a part of it.
logs.try.too_many: Many files match: Michel reads only some of them.
logs.errors.title: The errors Michel has seen
logs.errors.no_source: Michel does not read any log: it can say nothing about the errors of this server.
logs.errors.none: Michel saw no error in what it could read. If some files are “not read” above, it can say nothing about those.
logs.errors.unknown: Error whose name Michel does not know
logs.errors.truncated: There are {total} errors in all: Michel shows only the latest ones.
logs.errors.detail_help: To read the lines yourself, copy this command and paste it into the terminal (the command window) of your computer, or ask the person who looks after your server to run it. Michel does not run it: the lines stay on the server.
logs.errors.seen_hint: It is no longer counted among the new ones.
logs.errors.ignore: Stop warning me about this one
logs.errors.ignore_hint: Michel still counts it, but no longer sends you an alert for it.
logs.interval.title: How often does Michel read the logs?
logs.interval.hint: The more often, the sooner you hear of it. Michel can only read when your computer is on and Michel is running.
logs.interval.slow: With this interval, you may hear of an error more than 10 minutes after it happened.
logs.interval.manual_advanced: Michel reads the logs of this server only with the command "michel target logs read". Nobody is warned in between.
logs.interval.manual_simple: Michel reads the logs of this server only when you ask for it on the command line. Nobody is warned in between.
logs.alerts.title: Which errors warn you?
logs.alerts.hint: For each seriousness, choose how Michel warns you. “In the morning summary” means the error is added to the summary Michel sends you once a day.
logs.alerts.sms: Also warn me by text message for log errors
logs.alerts.sms_hint: Without this box, text messages stay reserved for flaws.
logs.channel.none: Michel will read this log, but nothing is set up to warn you: nobody will be told. Add a way to be warned (email, alert link (webhook) or desktop notification) in Michel's settings. Until then a badge stays on this server.
logs.channel.sms: A text message about a log error counts toward the same limit of 3 a day as flaw alerts: if errors send too many, flaws will no longer be able to warn you by text message.
logs.privacy.title: What Michel keeps on your computer
logs.privacy.intro: By default, Michel keeps only the seriousness, the kind of error, the file and the line of code concerned, how many times and the dates. It never keeps a line of the log. Each choice below starts with the one Michel recommends.
logs.privacy.store_text: Does Michel keep the text of the error message?
logs.privacy.alert_text: Is the text of the message put in alerts?
logs.privacy.alert_text_hint: Only possible if Michel keeps the text of messages.
logs.privacy.retention: How long does Michel keep the errors?
logs.privacy.retention_hint: After this time, Michel erases the errors it kept.
logs.privacy.away: A setting moves away from what Michel recommends.
logs.privacy.back: Go back to the recommended choices
logs.privacy.back_hint: Michel then erases at once the text it had kept.
logs.choice.store_text.yes: Yes, keep the message, without quoted text, numbers, IP addresses, emails and web addresses
logs.choice.alert_text.no: No, only the kind of error and the place
logs.choice.alert_text.yes: Yes, put the message in alerts, without quoted text, numbers, IP addresses, emails and web addresses
logs.deviation.store_text.title: Keep the text of error messages?
logs.deviation.alert_text.title: Put the text of messages in alerts?
logs.deviation.retention.title: Change how long Michel keeps the errors?
logs.deviation.other.title: Move away from what Michel recommends?
logs.deviation.health: This server holds health data. If text from its logs leaves the health data hosting (HDS), you are responsible for it. Michel does not stop you. Ask your data protection officer (DPO) if you are unsure.
logs.confirm.intro: This change moves away from what Michel recommends. Read what can happen before you go on.
logs.confirm.yes: Yes, I understand and I change it
logs.badge.no_channel: Nobody will be warned of log errors
logs.badge.deviation: Privacy: a setting moves away from the recommended choice
logs.read.never: Michel has not managed to read this log yet.
logs.read.off: Michel is not reading this log for now.
logs.purge.button: Erase the log data of this server
logs.purge.hint: Michel forgets all the errors and their counts it kept for this server, even those you chose to ignore. It keeps the list of your logs and your settings, and goes on reading them. Nothing is erased on the server.
logs.purge.title: Erase the log data of this server?
logs.purge.body: Michel will forget all the errors and their counts it kept for this server, even those you chose to ignore. You will not be able to go back. The list of your logs and your settings stay, and nothing is erased on the server.
logs.purge.done: Done: Michel erased the log data of this server.
logs.add.format_hint: If you are unsure, ask the person who looks after your server.
help.label: Help: {field}
help.server.host: The address of your server: a name (srv.example.test) or digits (192.0.2.10). Michel connects to it. If it is wrong, the connection fails or reaches another machine: at the next step, compare its fingerprint (the code that identifies it) with the one your host gives.
help.server.user: The account on the server that Michel connects with, for example deploy. It uses a key your computer keeps for you, never a password. A wrong name, or an account without your key: the connection is refused and nothing is changed.
help.server.port: The "port" is the number of the door through which the server accepts administration connections. It is almost always 22: change it only if your host gives you another. A wrong number: the connection fails and nothing is changed.
help.server.name: The name shown in Michel, so you can find your way, for example "Shop". It changes nothing on the server. Left empty, Michel uses the server address instead.
help.server.site: The address of your site (https://…), optional. After a fix, Michel opens it from your computer to see whether the site answers. Without it, Michel cannot see the site go down and undoes nothing for that. A wrong address looks like an outage: the fix is undone if it can be.
help.server.kind: The kind of hosting: VPS (a server of your own), shared (with other customers) or HDS (health data). Michel picks its rules from it and never sends an AI agent to an HDS. A health server taken for a VPS loses that safeguard.
help.server.env: The role of the server: production (the real site), preproduction (a copy to try things on) or development. Some rules apply to production only, and only a production server can have a linked preproduction. If you get it wrong, those rules do not apply.
help.server.level: What Michel does with a flaw: report it, explain it, prepare a fix (on request or by itself) or, at the last level, run it by itself when it follows your rules. The higher the level, the more Michel acts without your click. You can lower it any time.
help.server.auto: At the last level only. Michel fixes risky PHP settings by itself when foreseen, never a software update, after testing the configuration. It needs the site address and must be the one running the scripts. Ticked by mistake, a setting changes without your click.
help.server.executor: Who runs the fix scripts on the server. "You": Michel gives them to you. "Michel": it sends them after your approval, or alone if you allowed it, and follows each step. If the site has an address and stops answering, it undoes the fix, except a software update.
help.server.sudo: sudo = administrator rights, without a password. Michel uses it for a fix: simulate an update, run or undo the script, read back its backups. Never to check the server. At the last level, if he fixes on his own, without your click. Without sudo, you run the script.
help.server.interval: How often Michel checks this server by itself: from every 6 hours to once a week, or by hand only. The rarer it is, the older what you see can be. You can also click "Check now".
help.server.preprod: A preproduction is a copy of your server to try things before the real site. If you link one, Michel tries each fix there first and offers the production server only after a full success. Link only a real copy: the tries really happen there. Without a link, fixes are made here.
help.server.active: Ticked, Michel checks this server at the chosen pace and when you click "Check now". Unticked, it no longer checks it (the button is greyed out), no longer reads its logs and fixes nothing by itself: you get no new alert for this server.
help.server.fingerprint: The fingerprint is the code that identifies the server: it checks that Michel is talking to your machine. Compare it with the one your host gives before confirming. If it is wrong or changes later, someone may be posing as your server: do not confirm.
help.server.check: Michel connects to the server and looks at what is installed and set up. It changes nothing and does not use sudo. It can take a minute. The button is greyed out until the fingerprint is confirmed or while the server is turned off.
help.server.snapshot: A snapshot is a full copy of the server, made at your host. Make one before approving a software update: no script can undo it. Michel cannot check that you did it. If you say yes without one and the update breaks something, you have no way back.
help.project.level: Michel's level of action: report, explain, prepare a fix (on request or by itself) or, at the last level, put it by itself on a branch (a parallel copy of your code; yours does not move) if it follows your rules. Without AI consent it only explains.
help.project.auto: At the last level only. Michel creates the branch by itself if the fix touches only the list of libraries (the code your project borrows), with no big version jump or high risk, if the tests pass and the flaw is gone. Otherwise it waits for your click.
help.project.ai: Your consent for an AI agent (Claude, from Anthropic) to work on a copy of this project. The code it reads leaves your computer, including a key written in it, and the code it writes runs on that copy. Without consent, no agent starts: Michel explains, nothing more.
help.project.path: The full path of the folder, for example C:\Sites\my-site or /home/you/my-site. Michel writes nothing in it during a check: it reads its files. It refuses a system folder, a whole disk or your whole home folder.
help.project.name: The name shown in Michel. It is proposed from the folder and you can change it. This name changes nothing in your project. Two projects cannot have the same name.
help.decision.action: What you decide for this flaw: Fix (you plan to fix it), Put off (Michel brings it up again later) or Ignore (it does not concern you). Nothing in your project is changed, the decision is noted. Ignored by mistake: Michel only brings it up again if it changes.
help.decision.until: For Put off only: the day Michel brings the flaw up again, tomorrow at the earliest. Empty means in 30 days. It comes back sooner if the flaw changes. A past or badly written date is refused.
help.decision.why: One sentence to remind you why, 1000 characters at most. Optional, except for Ignore: without a reason, Michel refuses the decision. The reason is noted with it.
help.exposure.decision: Michel does not see the host's firewall: he cannot know whether this service is blocked. Write why there is nothing to do. Michel keeps your reason and does not check it. To change your mind, you will need a command: michel decide.
help.logs.path: The full location of the log file on the server, for example /var/log/php/error.log. The signs * and ? are allowed only in the file name. A path that does not start with / or that contains ".." is refused. A file that cannot be read is shown as "not read".
help.logs.format: The shape of the log lines: PHP errors, PostgreSQL, application, JSON or free text. If unsure, ask whoever looks after your server. With the wrong type, Michel does not understand the lines: "Try it" shows you before anything is watched.
help.logs.try: Michel reads this log once and shows what it would keep. Nothing is kept, and nothing is watched until you click "Read this log". If the result is empty or odd, do not click, and ask whoever looks after your server.
help.logs.interval: How often Michel reads the logs: from every minute to every 24 hours, or only when you ask. The rarer it is, the later you are told. Michel reads only while your computer is on and Michel is running.
help.logs.store_text: By default Michel does not keep the text of error messages, only their type, the place and the count. Keeping it helps you understand, but the text may hold private details, even cleaned. Michel asks you to confirm before keeping it.
help.logs.alert_text: Choose whether the error message is written in alerts. Possible only if Michel keeps the message text. The message is cleaned, but an alert leaves Michel for your e-mail or the alert link you set up: say no if unsure.
help.logs.retention: How many days Michel keeps errors, from 7 to 365 (90 advised). After that it erases them. Too short and you lose the history; too long and Michel keeps more on your computer.
help.logs.sms: Ticked, a log error can also send you a text message. Text messages are limited (3 a day by default), shared with flaw alerts: too many errors can stop a flaw from reaching you. Unticked, text messages stay for flaws.
help.fix.approve: Approve accepts the fix: Michel puts it on a separate branch, michel/fix-… (a parallel version of your code). Your current branch and your files do not move. Approved by mistake, it changes nothing until you bring it into your code.
help.fix.approve_server: Approve accepts this script. If you run it yourself, Michel gives it to you without connecting. If Michel runs it, it follows each step and, if the site has an address and stops answering, undoes it. A software update cannot be undone: only your snapshot takes you back.
help.fix.refuse: Refuse sets the proposal aside: nothing is applied, on your project or on your server. The flaw stays to fix and you can start a fix again. Saying why is optional.
help.settings.token: The token proves to Michel that this is you. This browser keeps a copy, and Michel the other. If it is missing or refused, go back to the terminal (the window where commands are typed) running "michel serve", the command that starts Michel, and reopen the link it shows.
help.settings.advanced: Also shows technical details (flaw identifiers, versions, commands, scripts) and a few settings for specialists. Only the display changes: what Michel does stays the same. Off at the start, remembered in this browser.
help.settings.theme: Light or dark, whichever you read best. Only the display changes, in this browser: what Michel does stays the same.
help.settings.lang: The language of Michel's pages, French or English. It is remembered in this browser. The language set in Michel's configuration may differ: it is not changed here.
fix.line.unknown: Michel does not know whether the fix went through. Check that your site works normally, then click "I checked the server".
fix.line.came_back: This flaw came back after the fix.
fix.done.came_back: This flaw came back after the fix: Michel sees it in your project again.
path.label: Where this flaw stands
path.step.fixed_ready: Ready, not yet in your code
path.step.expo_gone: Michel does not see this service open to all any more
path.means_none: Michel has no explanation for this flaw yet.
path.note.preparing: The agent is working on the copy. This can take a few minutes.
path.note.held.one: Michel found {n} possible key in your code. He waits for your answer before starting the agent.
path.note.held.other: Michel found {n} possible keys in your code. He waits for your answer before starting the agent.
path.note.withdrawn: The agent did not start: for this fix, nothing left your computer. Once the keys are out of these files and the change is saved in Git (a commit), start the fix again: Michel will search again.
path.hold.stopped: Michel stopped before starting the agent: for this fix, nothing left your computer. He only shows where to look, never the key itself.
path.hold.check: A key is a secret code that gives access to a service, like a password. Michel judges by the shape of what is written, and he can be wrong: look at these lines before you choose. A real key written in an unusual way can also get through without Michel stopping.
path.hold.if_continue.one: If you go on, the agent can read it and it reaches Anthropic, the company that makes this AI.
path.hold.if_continue.other: If you go on, the agent can read them and they reach Anthropic, the company that makes this AI.
path.hold.how.one: To remove it: take it out of this file, put it in a .env file (Michel never copies that file), save the change in Git (a commit), then start the fix again. Michel will search again. If it has already been used, change it where it is used too.
path.hold.how.other: To remove them: take them out of these files, put them in a .env file (Michel never copies that file), save the change in Git (a commit), then start the fix again. Michel will search again. If they have already been used, change them where they are used too.
path.hold.once: Your answer holds for this attempt only. Next time, Michel will search and ask again. Until you answer, no other fix of this project starts. With no answer after 14 days, Michel stops this fix and removes its copy: the agent does not start.
path.hold.gone: Michel no longer sees this flaw: there is no more reason to start the agent.
path.hold.continuing: Michel checks that nothing changed, then starts the agent…
path.note.by_rule: Your rule approved this fix: Michel creates its branch, a separate version of your code.
path.note.merge: The fix is ready on a separate branch (a separate version of your code), {branch}. It is not in your code yet.
path.note.checking: The fix ran on the server. Michel still has to check the result.
path.note.deploy: Fixed in your code. Remember to publish this version on your site: Michel does not know whether the online version is up to date.
path.note.deploy_unchecked: Fixed in your code: the flaw is gone. Michel saw it in your project (he could not check it before). Remember to publish this version on your site: Michel does not know whether the online version is up to date.
path.note.not_checked: Michel could not check this fix on his copy: he does not know whether the flaw is gone. He will look in your project, once the fix is in your code and your project has been checked again.
path.note.copy_not_confirmed: The flaw is gone from your project. Before your agreement, Michel could not confirm it on his working copy: so he does not mark this fix as verified.
path.note.came_back: This flaw came back after the fix: Michel sees it in your project again.
path.note.refused: You refused this proposal: nothing was applied.
path.note.refused_server: You refused this proposal: Michel ran nothing.
path.note.unknown: Michel does not know whether the fix went through. Check that your site works normally, then click "I checked the server".
path.note.superseded: A newer fix replaced this one.
path.note.failed: This attempt did not succeed: nothing was applied.
path.note.inconclusive: Michel could not confirm the fix.
path.note.vanished: Michel no longer sees this flaw in your project. None of his fixes did this: he does not know what made it go away.
path.note.vanished_after: Michel no longer sees this flaw in your project, and this attempt had nothing to do with it: he does not know what made it go away. There is nothing to start again.
path.note.no_site: Michel read the server again and no longer sees the flaw. This server has no site address: Michel did not check that your site still answers.
path.note.preparing_server: The fix is being prepared. Nothing changes on the server at this stage.
path.note.by_rule_server: Your rule approved this fix: Michel runs the script without waiting for your click, as soon as he can reach the server.
path.note.run_yours: Your approval is noted. It is up to you to run the script on the server, then tell Michel.
path.note.came_back_server: This flaw came back since the fix: Michel sees it again on this server.
path.note.unknown_server: Michel does not know what the script changed. Look at the server and your site, then click "I checked the server" in the proposal.
path.note.failed_server: This attempt did not succeed. Read the details of the fix before you start again.
path.note.vanished_server: Michel no longer sees this flaw on this server. None of his fixes had anything to do with it: he does not know what made it go away.
path.note.vanished_after_server: Michel no longer sees this flaw on this server, but this attempt did not succeed: he does not know what made it go away. There is nothing to start again.
plan.project.title: What the AI will do
plan.project.copy: An AI agent (Claude Code) works on a separate copy of your project: only the files of your last version saved in Git (your last commit), without your .env files or your keys in .pem or .key format. Careful: a key or password saved elsewhere in your project (in your code, a settings file, a key in another format) stays in the copy. Michel searches it for the keys he can recognise: if he finds one, the agent does not start until you answer. A key he does not recognise, the agent can read. Michel judges by the shape of what is written: a line that talks about a password without showing one does not stop the agent, and a real key of an unusual shape may not stop it either.
plan.project.update: Michel tries to update {package} to version {to} on this copy, then the agent adapts your code if needed.
plan.project.update_near: Michel tries to update {package} to version {to} or a close newer version on this copy, then the agent adapts your code if needed.
plan.project.update_any: Michel tries to update {package} on this copy, then the agent adapts your code if needed.
plan.project.search: Michel knows of no ready-made update: the agent looks for a fix on this copy.
plan.project.update_agent: Michel does not run this update himself here: the agent makes it in the files of this copy.
plan.project.tests: Michel then tries to install and run your tests on this copy, then looks for the flaw again. If the tests cannot run, the proposal tells you.
plan.project.no_tests: Michel looks for the flaw again on this copy. Your tests will not run: no test command is set for this project.
plan.project.no_install: This project uses yarn or pnpm, tools Michel does not run: nothing is installed and your tests do not run.
plan.project.no_install_kind: For this kind of flaw, Michel installs nothing on this copy: your tests will not run.
plan.project.approval: Nothing reaches your code without your agreement: if you approve, Michel creates a branch, a separate version of your code. He never mixes it into your code and puts nothing online: your site does not change.
plan.project.approval_auto: With your rule, a small update can go alone if it meets all the conditions, including: tests passed, flaw gone from the copy, no code file touched. Michel then creates its branch, a separate version of your code, without asking you. The rest waits for your agreement. He never mixes it into your code and puts nothing online: your site does not change.
plan.project.self_start: At this level, once you have agreed for this project, the agent can start without you clicking. If Michel finds a key in the code, the agent waits for your answer.
plan.project.data: This AI is external: what it reads of the copy goes to Anthropic, including a key saved in these files, if Michel did not recognise it or if you chose to go on. Michel asks for your agreement once per project.
plan.project.health: This project holds health data: no AI works on it.
plan.project.report_only: This project is set to "Report": Michel prepares nothing. You can change this setting on its card.
plan.project.no_git: This folder is not a Git repository (a folder that keeps the history of your files): Michel cannot prepare a fix, but he explains the flaw to you.
plan.server.title: What Michel will do
plan.server.who: Michel prepares a script (a series of commands) himself from his rules, without AI. Preparing changes nothing on the server.
plan.server.who_auto: Michel prepares a script (a series of commands) himself from his rules, without AI. With your rule, he can run it on the server by himself, right after, with administrator rights (root), without waiting for your click.
plan.server.no_ready: Michel has no ready-made fix for this flaw.
plan.server.no_copy: A server has no separate copy: this script will act on the server itself. You can read it before you approve.
plan.server.no_copy_auto: This script will act on the server itself. With your rule, you may not have time to read it first.
plan.server.preprod: This script is first tried on your preprod {name} (your test server), with that preprod's settings. The fix for this server is prepared only once it is proven there.
plan.server.checks: The script first keeps a backup of the settings file, tests the configuration when it can and restarts PHP (the program that runs your site) if needed. Michel then checks your site and reads the server again. If a step fails after the change, the script tries to put the files back.
plan.server.no_site: The script first keeps a backup of the settings file and tests the configuration when it can. If a step fails after the change, it tries to put the files back. Without a site address, Michel does not check that your site still answers: he only reads the server again. If your site goes down, Michel does not see it and puts nothing back.
plan.server.package: Michel first simulates the update. No script can undo it: before you approve, he will ask you to make a snapshot (a full backup of the server) at your host.
plan.server.package_no_site: Without a site address, Michel does not check that your site still answers after the update: he only reads the server again.
plan.server.no_tests: Your application's tests are not run.
plan.server.approval_user: Nothing changes on this server without your agreement: after you approve, you run the script yourself.
plan.server.approval_michel: Nothing changes on this server without your agreement: after you approve, Michel sends this script to it over his secure connection (SSH).
plan.server.root: The script runs there with the server's administrator rights.
plan.server.choice_user: For now, you run the script yourself. If you would rather have Michel run it for you, set "Who runs the scripts" to "Michel" in the settings of {name}, before you validate.
plan.server.choice_user_root: For now, you run the script yourself, with the server's administrator rights (called "root"). If you would rather have Michel run it for you, set "Who runs the scripts" to "Michel" in the settings of {name}, and also allow "sudo" (the command that gives those administrator rights, without a password). Michel runs nothing before you click Validate.
plan.server.approval_auto: With your rule, a PHP setting on Michel's list is fixed without a click, if every condition is met: the script then runs with the server's administrator rights. A software update always waits for your agreement.
plan.server.approval_user_preprod: Nothing changes on your preprod {name} without your agreement: after you approve, you run the script there yourself.
plan.server.approval_michel_preprod: Nothing changes on your preprod {name} without your agreement: after you approve, Michel sends this script there over his secure connection.
plan.server.approval_auto_preprod: With your rule on your preprod {name}, a PHP setting on Michel's list is fixed there without a click, if every condition is met: the script then runs with that preprod's administrator rights. A software update always waits for your agreement.
plan.server.self_prepare: At this level, after a check of the server, Michel also tries to prepare the script by himself, without a click.
plan.server.agent: If Michel has no planned fix, an AI agent can study the case, if you have accepted it. The agent never connects to the server and cannot run anything. It sees the list of what Michel noted on the server, without what Michel recognises as secret.
plan.server.hds: This server hosts health data: no AI agent works on it.
plan.server.hds_preprod: Your preprod {name} hosts health data: no AI agent works on it, so none for this server either.
plan.server.report_only: This server is set to "Report": Michel prepares nothing.
plan.exposure: Michel cannot close this service and runs nothing.
expo.how: Ask the person who manages the server, or your host, to keep this service to the server itself, or to block it in the firewall (the filter that decides who can connect to it). If it is kept to the server, run a check: Michel will say whether he still sees it open to all. If it is only blocked in the firewall, Michel will still see it open: he checks from inside the server. In that case, click "I know, it is blocked or wanted".
expo.how_no_finding: That button is not there yet: it appears after the next check, once Michel has noted this service as a flaw.
expo.ask: To give this person: access number {number} (the number used to reach this service).
expo.check_how: Ask the person who manages the server which program uses access number {number} (the number used to reach this service), and whether it should stay open to all.
expo.heading: Exposure
expo.title.none: {server}: Michel sees no service open to all from the server
expo.title.one: {server}: {n} service reachable unless a firewall blocks it
expo.title.other: {server}: {n} services reachable unless a firewall blocks them
expo.title.not_read: {server}: Michel could not read yet which services wait to be contacted
expo.title.load_failed: {server}: Michel could not show this part
expo.sub: A service is a program on your server that waits to be contacted. A firewall is the filter that decides who can connect to it. Michel looks from inside the server.
expo.col.not_read: Not read: Michel does not know what is here.
expo.col.none: Michel sees none from the server.
expo.reserved.server: Reserved to the server: it answers only the server itself.
expo.reserved.private: Reserved to the private network: only the machines on that network can reach it.
expo.firewall.name: Firewall of the host
expo.firewall.note: Michel does not see it from the server. A service listed "open to all" may be blocked by this firewall, and Michel does not know.
expo.udp.name: Services in UDP
expo.udp.note: Michel reads only the services in TCP, the most common type. The services in UDP, the other type, do not appear here.
expo.service.admin_note: Normal. This is how Michel connects. Protect it with a key.
expo.service.admin_other_note: This is often how a server is administered, but Michel does not connect this way. See whether it should stay open to all.
expo.service.admin_mapped_note: Normal. This is where Michel connects, even if you reach it through another number (a redirection). It should only accept a key to log in.
expo.service.database_note: Nobody outside needs to reach it.
expo.service.cache_note: A fast memory that sites often use. Nobody outside needs to reach it.
expo.service.other_note: Michel does not know what program this is.
expo.shared: On shared hosting, these services may be the host's or other customers': Michel does not make findings of them.
expo.shared_note: It may be the host's or another customer's.
expo.kept: Michel noted a finding on this service at an earlier read. It stays as long as he sees it open to all and you have said nothing.
expo.decision.open: I know, it is blocked or wanted
expo.decision.title: {service}: blocked or wanted
expo.decision.body: Michel keeps your reason in his audit log (the list of what was done). He does not check what you write. The service stays in its column, and leaves your to-do list. To change your mind later, you will need a command.
expo.decision.which: This is access number {number} (the number used to reach this service).
expo.decision.why_hint: Required. For example: blocked by my host's firewall.
expo.decision.done: Noted. Michel did not check it.
expo.decided: You said: {why} Michel did not check it.
expo.decided_undo: To change your mind, type this command in a terminal (the window where commands are typed): michel decide {id} defer --for 1d. It replaces what you said.
expo.closed_title: No longer seen open to all
expo.closed_hint: This is neither a fix nor a verification: the service may have moved or stopped. Michel only knows that he does not see it any more.
expo.closed: {service}: Michel does not see this service open to all any more.
expo.closed_unread: {service}: at his last complete read, Michel did not see this service open to all any more. Today, he does not know.
expo.closed_date: Last time Michel saw this service open to all: {date}.
expo.load_failed: This says nothing about what is open on the server.
expo.flaws_above: The only flaws Michel noted on this server are in the Exposure part, just above.
plain.server_package: A piece of software installed on this server has a known flaw. Updating it fixes the flaw.
plain.server_unfixed: A piece of software installed on this server has a known flaw.
git.manual.lead: You still have to bring this fix into your code. Open a terminal (the window where you type commands) in your project's folder, check that you are on your main version (often called main; the command git branch --show-current gives the name of the one you are on), paste this command and press Enter.
git.manual.next: Then, in My projects, click "Check this project".
git.manual.copy_failed: Copy failed: select the command by hand.
git.question: Is your project also on a site where code is shared (GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, for example)?
git.why: If so, Michel can send the fix to that site in one click, and you accept it there, with no command to type. If you don't know, answer "I don't know": Michel sends nothing and tells you what to do by hand. Nothing is attached without your yes, and you can change your answer any time.
git.suggest.known: Michel read a {provider} address in your project: {display}. That suggests yes, but your answer is what counts.
git.suggest.other: Michel read the address of a service it does not recognise in your project: {display}. It may be a code-sharing site. If you don't know, answer "I don't know".
git.suggest.none: Michel finds no code-sharing site address in your project. That suggests no.
git.suggest.several: Your project has several addresses and none is called origin: Michel does not know which to choose and cannot attach it.
git.suggest.unsupported: The address read in your project is not an https or SSH (secure connection) address Michel can use: it cannot attach it.
git.credential: The address saved in your project holds a password or a token. Michel does not show it, keep it or use it. If sending fails, save your access another way, with your usual Git tool.
git.yes_detail: By saying yes, you allow Michel to contact {host}, only when you click a button. It uses the Git access already set up on this computer and stores no password.
git.title: The service that holds your code
git.state.not_attached: Not attached. After a fix, you will have to merge it yourself with Git, that is, bring it into your code.
git.state.changed: Your project's address changed since you agreed ({display}). Michel sends nothing until you answer again.
git.state.changed_gone: Your project's address changed since you agreed. Michel sends nothing until you answer again.
git.none: This folder is not a Git repository (a folder that keeps the history of your files). Michel can check it and explain its flaws. He cannot prepare a fix: he works from the last version Git kept. Michel does not create a repository for you.
git.none_how: If your project has a Git repository, add its main folder, the one that holds the .git folder. Otherwise, ask the person who manages your code.
git.empty: This Git repository has no saved version yet. Michel can check it, but needs a first saved version (commit) to prepare a fix.
git.unreadable: Michel cannot read this folder for now.
git.unreadable_yes: To answer yes, Michel must be able to read this folder. You can still answer no or "I don't know".
git.saved.yes: Your saved answer: yes. Michel sends nothing while it cannot read this folder.
git.saved.unknown: Your saved answer: I don't know.
git.manual.attach: If your project is on GitHub, Bitbucket or GitLab, you can attach it: you will have no more commands to type.
git.push.other: Send the fix to your Git service
git.push.lead: Michel sends only the branch {branch}, a separate version of your code. If you have changes on this computer that you have not sent to the site yet, they travel with this branch. Your main version on the site stays as it is.
git.push.way_out: If sending does not work, click "Change my answer" below, then "No": Michel will give you a command to copy instead.
git.push.done.known: Fix sent to {provider}. If it is not accepted yet, do it on the site.
git.push.done.other: Fix sent. If the branch {branch} is not merged yet (brought into your code), ask for it on your service.
git.push.already: This fix is already on the service: Michel sent nothing again.
git.merge.lead: A merge request is what brings the fix into your code. This link opens a new tab: first create the request (the button is often called "Create pull request" or "Create merge request"), then accept it ("Merge"). This page stays open.
git.merge.no_link: Michel has no safe link to this page. On the site, look for the branch {branch} and ask to merge it, that is, to bring it into your code.
git.after: Once the fix is accepted on the site, click "Update my folder": Michel can then verify it.
git.update.lead: Michel brings to your computer what was accepted on the site, without mixing anything. If that is not possible, it leaves your files alone and tells you why.
git.update.wait: Michel is fetching what is new from the site. It can take a moment: wait here, the button comes back as soon as it is done.
git.update.done: Your folder is up to date. Michel starts the check.
git.update.done_no_check: Your folder is up to date, but Michel could not start the check.
git.update.none: Nothing new on the site. If the fix is still waiting, accept it, then try again.
git.update.checked: Check finished. Michel cannot say yet that the fix is in your folder. If it is still waiting on the site, accept it, then click "Update my folder" again.
git.update.check_self: Your folder already has the fix, or the check did not finish? In My projects, click "Check this project".
help.project.git: What it is for: sending a fix to the site where your code lives. Yes if you see your project there, otherwise no, or "I don't know". If you get it wrong, change your answer: nothing is sent without a click from you.
